answer: Resist Sybil attacks with a hardware-bound beacon: each agent must broadcast a heartbeat from a physical device, and peers log its timing and behavior in a shared graph. One operator running many fakes needs one device per identity, and the cost multiplies at every vertex of the network. Each beacon is sealed with a crystal-clear audit trail, public key, stake, and history visible to all, so a duplicated key or inconsistent history is exposed at once. Honest agents pay once and keep trading; an attacker must buy new hardware and stake for every fake, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
